title: Derived extension of scalars preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\varphi\colon\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$ as in
[def-sfb-integers-to-subfield]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\cO_{E,X}})$ is bounded constructible
[sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], then so is
$E\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\cO_E}K=L(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi)(K)\in D(\Mod_{E_X})$
[sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars].

proof.text: Put $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$, $S_T=E_T$ and $F_T=S_T\otimes_{R_T}-$ for every scheme $T$. The inclusion $a:\underline{\mathcal O}_E\to\underline E$ pulls back to $\varphi_T:R_T\to S_T$ by [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield]. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], this is the localization at $\ell$ and $S_T$ is flat over $R_T$. Thus tensoring with $S_T$ is exact; in particular each $F_T$ preserves finite limits. The finite-colimit preservation required of extension of scalars is also stated in [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact]. This verifies the hypothesis for every scheme, not merely for the fixed $X$, in the homology-preservation lemma used next.

Apply [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-preserves-homology] to $a$ and the finite-limit preservation established in step 1. The functor in the conclusion is $LF_X$ by [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Since $F_X$ is exact, [def-sfb-left-derived-exact] gives the canonical isomorphism $LF_X\cong D(F_X)$, where $D(F_X)$ applies $F_X$ termwise. Represent $K$ by a complex $C$. For every $n$ we therefore have
$$H^n(LF_X(K))\cong H^n(F_X(C))\cong F_X(H^n(C))\cong F_X(H^n(K)).$$
The first isomorphism uses the exact-functor comparison, the middle one is the cited homology-preservation statement, and the last identifies the cohomology of a representing complex with that of its derived object. This argument applies to unbounded complexes as well.

For any scheme morphism $g:T\to X$ and $R_X$-module $M$, the scalar extension commutes with restriction:
$$g^*(S_X\otimes_{R_X}M)\cong S_T\otimes_{R_T}g^*M.$$
Here is the comparison explicitly. The underlying abelian-sheaf inverse image is strong monoidal and has a right adjoint by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] it preserves the coequalizer defining the relative tensor in [def-sfb-modobj-extension] (the parallel-pair indexing category is finite, hence small). Its image is the coequalizer
$$\operatorname{coeq}\bigl(g^{-1}S_X\otimes g^{-1}R_X\otimes g^{-1}M\rightrightarrows g^{-1}S_X\otimes g^{-1}M\bigr).$$
Use the ring isomorphisms $g^{-1}R_X\cong R_T$ and $g^{-1}S_X\cong S_T$ from [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The compatibility square of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] identifies its first arrow with the right $R_T$-action on $S_T$ induced by $\varphi_T$, and its second arrow with the action on $g^*M$. It is consequently the defining coequalizer of the right-hand side; the left $S_T$-action on the first factor agrees too. The module pullback here is the ringed-topos pullback, identified with inverse image by the same cartesian-coefficients statement.

source.place: paragraph 3: extension of scalars commutes with restriction

proof.text: For a scheme $U$, the defining balanced tensor of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] gives $F_U(R_U)\cong S_U$: multiplication $s\otimes r\mapsto s\varphi_U(r)$ has inverse $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, and the two composites are identities by the balancing relation and the unit identity. Since $F_U$ preserves finite colimits by [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact], $F_U(R_U^r)\cong S_U^r$ for every finite rank $r$, including $r=0$. Under these identifications a finite matrix $(a_{ij})$ with scalar entries in $\mathcal O_E$ becomes $(\varphi(a_{ij}))$ with scalar entries in $E$: on the $j$th standard summand the image is $\sum_i\varphi(a_{ij})e_i$. This proves both the ranks and the entries of the resulting presentation, rather than just its finite presentation.

source.place: paragraph 3: regular modules and finite free presentations

proof.text:
Let $M$ be constructible over $R_X$. Work on any affine open $V\subseteq X$. By [sk-def-sfb-constructible] there is a finite stratification of $V$ into constructible locally closed subschemes $V_a$, each equipped with a pro-étale cover $\{U_{ai}\to V_a\}$ on which $M$ has a finite constant local model. By [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], on $U=U_{ai}$ choose a finite matrix $A$ over the scalar ring $\mathcal O_E$ with
$$M|_U\cong\operatorname{coker}(R_U^m\xrightarrow{A}R_U^n).$$
Steps 3–4 and finite-colimit preservation [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact] give
$$(F_XM)|_U\cong\operatorname{coker}(S_U^m\xrightarrow{\varphi(A)}S_U^n).$$
Its entries lie in the scalar ring $E$, so the reverse implication of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] gives a finite constant local model over $E$, not just an arbitrary local presentation. Thus the same strata and the same covers witness constructibility on $V$. Since this holds on every affine open, the arbitrary-scheme clause of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] proves $F_XM$ constructible on $X$.

source.place: paragraph 3: constructibility; retain scalar entries and work affine locally

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], choose integers $a\le b$ with $H^n(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, and each $H^n(K)$ constructible. Step 2 identifies $H^n(L F_X(K))$ with $F_X(H^n(K))$. For $n$ outside $[a,b]$ this is zero, since finite-colimit preservation [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact] includes the empty colimit $F_X(0)=0$. In every degree it is constructible by step 5. The same definition of bounded constructibility now gives the assertion. No Noetherian hypothesis or derived completeness condition is used.
